title: Fringe Show 5: Diva Live from Hell ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ @Edinburgh Festival Fri...
transcript: If you gave Dear Evan Hansen the oh Mary treatment, that would essentially be diva live from hell. Like, that's the best way I know to describe this show. Diva live from hell is a one person show starring the brilliant Luke Bear, who is so freaking funny in this. And the premise of this show is that essentially, this teenager has died and gone to hell, and his punishment in hell is to reenact, cabaret style, uh, his final weeks on earth that involve some high school theater drama that results in the death of a student. Well, I guess technically two students, because he's also dead. The premise already insane. What really seals the deal on the show, however, is Luke Bauer's incredible character work. He is so funny, and he plays every single one of the characters in this show with such unique characterization of each of them. Like, he goes from playing the flamboyant theater kid to the dumb jock to the mousy stage manager with, like, hilarious clarity. And then on top of that, is just a fantastic musical theater performer and performs these absolutely fantastic musical numbers with, like, full choreography. And the way that he interacts with the audience and plays off the audience is also freaking hilarious. Like, he was making the band crack up. The only criticism that I have to say about this show is that it did feel like it started to get a little bit of pacing issues. By the end of it, I just wanted the end to speed up, but just a little bit. Especially with how fast paced the beginning of the show is. It didn't quite finish at the same level that it started, and I needed to to actually like, finish at a higher level. But that didn't prevent this but from still being one of my favorite shows at the fringe. This is an absolute must see, especially for Luke Bears performance. This is currently playing at fringe at Underbelly Cowgate. And if you go see this, there is the diary of a Gay Disaster right after, which is going to be my next review. Which is also hilarious. And they make the perfect companion pieces to each other, so I highly recommend going to see both if you can.
